summary.text: 差 is commonly used for difference, mismatch, and unevenness. Its received traditional analysis explains the graph as mismatch, while early bronze forms have competing interpretations, so one origin cannot be assigned to every form and reading.

formation.text: The received Shuowen analysis divides 差 into 左 and 𠂹 and connects the whole to mismatch. A modern paleographic proposal distinguishes early bronze forms: one may depict bundled fuel and relate to 㷢; another is interpreted as misaligned hands, with 左 serving as a phonetic note. These analyses do not establish a single formation or sequence. The familiar story of rubbing wheat between the hands is disputed, and the identification of 來 within 差 is not established.

components.text: In the received analysis, 左 is one part of 差. A separate proposal treats it as a phonetic note in one distinct early form; that role is not established for every form. 左 itself developed from a pictograph of a left hand, 𠂇, with 工 added in later bronze forms. This history of 左 does not prove that early 差 contained the complete graph.

sound.text: For the proposed phonetic role in one early form, Baxter–Sagart reconstructs 左 as *tsˤa[j]ʔ and 差 chā as *tsʰraj. Their initials differ, so this is a related sound-series proposal, not an identical reading; the role is form-specific.

components.text: 𠂹 is the second part in the received analysis of 差, whose whole meaning is glossed as mismatch. Later lexicographic interpretation connects this form with divergence, but its independent function within the graph is not established.

In one proposed analysis of a distinct early form, the lower structure depicts two hands out of alignment. This interpretation concerns that early form, not a settled component of modern 差 or of every ancient form.

history.text: The selected Western Zhou bronze-style image is a modern redraw associated with 同簋蓋, not an artifact photograph. Early bronze forms are debated, and the specialist account reports no oracle-bone example in the materials it considered; these facts do not show a linear path to the modern form.

The received Shuowen account analyzes 差 as 左 plus 𠂹 and glosses it as mismatch. Later annotation discusses divergence, unevenness, and selection, but this traditional analysis does not directly confirm the earliest graphic form.

A modern proposal connects one form, interpreted as bundled fuel, with 㷢, glossed as a bundle of charcoal. The cited bronze use of 㷢 writes 差 loanwise. The further proposal that the early 差 picture named that fuel is tentative; the spoken name and pronunciation of the pictured object are not established, so the proposed sound-based borrowing cannot be verified.

uncertainties.text: The wheat-rubbing account identifies shapes as 來 and a hand, but paleographic analysis disputes that reading. Resemblance to 來 or 羊 does not establish either as a component of 差.

Early bronze forms have competing interpretations, and some have also been read as 樹. Neither the traditional analysis nor the bundled-fuel and misaligned-hands proposals establishes one origin for all forms and readings.
Pronunciation reconstructions depend on the reading and reconstruction system. The proposed 左 sound relationship is not an exact match and is not established across all readings of 差.

Textual evidence attests selection, unevenness, mismatch or error, and a ritual washing verb, but does not establish a complete chronology or semantic path among them. The composition dates of the cited Odes and Xunzi passages are unresolved.

senses.period: Han lexicographic account; graph attested in Western Zhou bronzes
senses.text: The received Shuowen gloss and analysis record 差 as mismatch. This is a historical lexicographic interpretation, not necessarily the earliest spoken meaning.

senses.period: early textual use; precise composition date unresolved
senses.text: In the transmitted Odes passage ‘既差我馬,’ 差 is read as selecting the horses. This early attested use does not prove that selection was the word’s original meaning.

senses.period: early compound use; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: The compound 參差 is attested in an Odes line and glossed as uneven or irregular. This attests the compound meaning, but does not date the standalone sense or show that it developed from mismatch.
Modern dictionaries record difference and distinction among the senses of 差. When these became associated with mismatch is unresolved.

senses.period: historical and current; earliest dating unresolved
senses.text: Error and discrepancy are recorded senses. A pre-imperial Xunzi passage uses 差 in a divergence- or error-related context, though the precise nuance is uncertain.

senses.period: historical and current; earliest dating unresolved
senses.text: A distinct reading tradition records selecting, dispatching, and a dispatched person or task. The evidence does not establish a semantic path from mismatch or difference to these uses.
A ritual passage uses 差 for rinsing, glossed as rice-washing. This is a distinct reading and lexical use, with no established connection to difference or the proposed wheat-rubbing origin.

senses.period: historical and current through the spelling 瘥; dating unresolved
senses.text: A separate reading tradition records recovery, also later written 瘥. No semantic transition linking it to the other senses is established.

developments.text: Later lexicographic interpretation associates mismatch and divergence with unevenness, but a historical transition between them is not established.
Lexicographic explanation and textual interpretation relate these meanings, but how or when error developed from mismatch is unresolved.

limitations.text: The listed historical and modern senses do not establish their chronology. Dates for the cited textual compositions are unresolved, and several reading groups have no supported transition connecting them.
A tentative borrowing proposal links a pictured fuel bundle to 㷢, but the bundle’s ancient spoken name and pronunciation are unverified, so sound cannot confirm why its graph was reused for 差.

overview.text: 差 commonly expresses difference, mismatch, or unevenness. Its traditional analysis connects the graph with mismatch; early bronze forms also have competing interpretations, and the popular wheat-rubbing explanation is disputed.

components.text: 左 appears in the traditional analysis and is proposed as a sound note in one distinct early form; that proposal does not cover every form of 差.
𠂹 is the second part in the traditional analysis, later connected with mismatch and divergence.
One competing analysis sees two misaligned hands in a distinct early form, not as established parts of modern 差.

relationships.text: One analysis proposes 左 as a phonetic note in a distinct early form of 差; the role is form-specific and not established for every form.
One competing analysis interprets the lower structure in a distinct early form as two misaligned hands; it does not claim modern 差 contains 𠂇 as a component.
